clue.text: North African soldier's run away twice

parts.note: to desert is to run away from duty
the second 'run away': to rat is to abandon one's side

explanation.surface: A soldier in North Africa is reported to have fled not once but two times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twice' tells you to find two different words for 'run away'; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Desert Rats was the nickname of the British 7th Armoured Division, who fought in the North African campaign of the Second World War.

clue.text: Abode we left in outskirts of district

indicators.note: the earlier words are placed inside the edges of the following word
the outskirts of a place are its edges, so only the first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the two edge letters of district
taken as written
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone describes a home they once shared, out on the edge of a district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abode' looks like a noun for a home, but it is the past tense of the verb abide.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide is an old verb for living somewhere, so its past tense abode matches the past tense of dwell.

clue.text: Husband comes in, somewhat lacking

indicators.note: something that comes in enters, so this letter goes inside the following phrase

parts.note: 'sort of' means somewhat or to some degree
H is the standard abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A husband walks in, seeming a bit lacking.
explanation.walkthrough: H goes in after the S of SORT OF.
explanation.definitionFit: To be short of something is to have too little of it, which is what lacking means.

clue.text: Go off clutching old turnip, perhaps

indicators.note: to clutch something is to hold it tightly, so the first word holds the next inside it

parts.note: food that goes off rots
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Something going bad while holding an ancient turnip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' signals a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnip is a vegetable grown for its swollen edible taproot, so it is one example of a root.

clue.text: Storyteller raised bar

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word makes it read upwards from the bottom

parts.note: a liar tells stories in the sense of untruths

explanation.surface: A storyteller lifted a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A rail is a horizontal bar, as in a towel rail or a fence rail.

clue.text: Travelling magi listen for temporal proclamation

indicators.note: letters that are travelling are on the move and will not stay in their printed order

parts.note: the fodder, ten letters

explanation.surface: The wandering Wise Men tune in for an announcement about the times.
explanation.walkthrough: The magi were the travelling Wise Men of the Nativity, which hides the anagram signal in plain sight.
explanation.definitionFit: A time signal is a broadcast announcement of the exact hour, such as the BBC pips, so it proclaims the time.

clue.text: Immoral city doctors in recession hosting party

indicators.note: something in recession is going backwards, so the word is read in reverse
a host has guests inside, so the reversed word holds the next one

parts.note: MO is medical officer, a doctor; plural MOS
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Doctors in an economic slump throw a party in a wicked city.
explanation.walkthrough: SOM, the doctors turned round, takes DO after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodom is the biblical city destroyed for its wickedness, so it is the classic immoral city.

clue.text: Sweet dishes often full of lumps?

definitions.text: Sweet dishes often full of lumps?

parts.words: Sweet dishes often full of lumps
parts.note: surface reading: lumpy desserts, like a badly made custard or rice pudding

parts.words: Sweet dishes often full of lumps
parts.note: setter's reading: tableware containers holding sugar, often in lump form

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet dishes' sounds like puddings, but here the dishes are containers holding something sweet, and the lumps are sugar cubes.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowls for serving sugar at the table are dishes for something sweet, and they often hold sugar lumps.

clue.text: Very determined group joining late

indicators.note: joining means attaching, so the first word is tacked on after the second

parts.note: the late So-and-so is dead
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A resolute group signing up after the deadline.
explanation.definitionFit: To be dead set on something is an idiom for being utterly determined to do it.

clue.text: On the Paris underground Zurich financier reported speed regulator

parts.note: the Métro is the Paris underground railway

indicators.note: a report is something told, so we want the sound of the word rather than its spelling

parts.note: 'the gnomes of Zurich' is a nickname for Swiss bankers

explanation.surface: A Swiss banker on the Paris Métro is said to have set the pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gnomes of Zurich' is a stock phrase for Swiss bankers; the silent G drops out when spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: A metronome is a device musicians use to keep a steady tempo, so it regulates speed.

clue.text: He hopes for more from his overseas post

definitions.text: He hopes for more from his overseas post

parts.words: He hopes for more from his overseas post
parts.note: surface reading: someone hoping for more letters from abroad

parts.words: He hopes for more from his overseas post
parts.note: setter's reading: someone who moves abroad to a job hoping to earn more money

explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' looks like mail, but it is a job, and 'more' is more pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who moves to another country to improve their earnings is called an economic migrant.

clue.text: Small child finally broke betting system

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the following word, its closing letter

parts.note: the closing letter of broke

explanation.surface: A toddler at last broke the betting system.
explanation.definitionFit: The tote, short for totalisator, is a pool betting system used at racecourses.

clue.text: Journalists entering teashop regularly for coffee

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so the first word goes into the letters that follow
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of teashop
journalists collectively are the press

explanation.surface: Reporters keep dropping into a tearoom for a coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: PRESS goes in after the first two kept letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Espresso is strong black coffee made by forcing steam through ground beans.

clue.text: Elf uses mobile patterns in grass

parts.note: an elf is a kind of fairy
to ring someone is to phone them

explanation.surface: A little magical being makes calls on a mobile phone.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English a mobile is a mobile phone, and to ring is to call.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairy rings are circles of darker grass or mushrooms caused by fungus, a pattern seen on lawns.

clue.text: Social girl unfortunately smokes

indicators.note: something that has turned out unfortunately has gone wrong, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: the fodder, ten letters

explanation.surface: A sociable young woman sadly has a smoking habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Cigarillos are small thin cigars, so they are things one smokes; 'smokes' is a plural noun here.

clue.text: Contents of avant-garde flat in Greenwich far from inspiring

indicators.note: contents are what lies inside, so the answer sits within the following words

parts.note: runs across the end of avant-garde, all of flat and in, and the start of Greenwich

explanation.surface: The furnishings of an arty flat in Greenwich are underwhelming.
explanation.walkthrough: Greenwich is a district of south-east London.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deflating lets the air out of your spirits, so it is the opposite of inspiring, which literally means breathing in.

clue.text: Hesitant fellows standing in for protester's two sons

indicators.note: one who stands in for another takes their place, so one pair of letters replaces another

parts.note: a dissident protests against the authorities
F is the abbreviation for fellow; doubled for the plural
S is the abbreviation for son, twice

explanation.surface: Uncertain men take the place of an activist's two boys.
explanation.definitionFit: A diffident person lacks confidence and so holds back, which is being hesitant.

clue.text: Better party rejected initially

indicators.note: initially here means at the start, so that word is placed first rather than in clue order

parts.note: something rejected is out, ruled out
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A political party was turned down at the first attempt to improve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' looks like a first-letter signal, but it only says which piece comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To better someone, as a verb, is to surpass them, which is what outdo means.

clue.text: Not so many sheep in France

indicators.note: in places the first word inside the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: FR is the abbreviation for France
a ewe is a female sheep

explanation.surface: French farms have a smaller flock than they used to.
explanation.definitionFit: Fewer is the comparative of few, meaning a smaller number of, so not so many.

clue.text: New recipe for stews in Observer

indicators.note: a new recipe remakes the ingredients a different way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, seven letters

explanation.surface: A newspaper food column offers a fresh way to make casseroles.
explanation.walkthrough: The Observer is a British Sunday newspaper, which makes the surface read like a cookery column.
explanation.definitionFit: A witness is a person who observes an event, so it is a synonym for observer.

clue.text: A cover, we hear, fitted on tap

indicators.note: what we hear is the spoken form, so the words are pronounced rather than spelt

parts.note: a veil is a cover for the face
fitted for a task means able to do it

explanation.surface: Someone describes a cover that is fitted to a tap.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first part is a sound-alike; 'fitted' gives its piece directly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on tap is ready whenever wanted, as beer from a tap is, so it is available.

clue.text: Nasty pong drifting along Italian town

indicators.note: something drifting wanders off course, so these letters stray from their order

parts.note: BO is body odour, an unpleasant smell
the letters of along rearranged

explanation.surface: A bad smell wafts through the streets of an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pong' is British slang for a bad smell. 'Nasty pong drifting' looks like a seven-letter anagram, but only the last word is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Bologna is a city in northern Italy; 'town' is used loosely for any settlement.

clue.text: One omitted from stopgap eleven brought back to join in …

indicators.note: omitted means left out, so that letter is removed from the following word

parts.note: an interim arrangement is a stopgap
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: bringing something back returns it the other way, so it is read in reverse

parts.note: XI is eleven in Roman numerals, also a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: A makeshift team is recalled after one player drops out, to join in.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links into the next clue but is only for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To intermix is to mix together, so it means to join in or blend.

clue.text: … aims to retire, avoiding a strenuous spell of work

indicators.note: to retire is to withdraw backwards, so the word is read in reverse
avoiding something means leaving it out, so the letter named is removed

parts.note: goals are aims
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone aiming to retire and escape a hard stint at work.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis continues the previous clue's surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: A slog is a long stretch of hard, tiring work.

clue.text: Nerd getting to grips with right language

indicators.note: grappling with something means holding it, so the first word wraps around the next

parts.note: a geek is a nerd
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A swot finally tackles the correct language.
explanation.definitionFit: Greek is the language of Greece, ancient and modern.

clue.text: Dry tart chef originally rejected

indicators.note: something rejected is thrown out, so that letter is removed

parts.note: acrid means sharp or bitter, as tart does

indicators.note: originally means at the origin or start, so only the first letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of chef

explanation.surface: The cook threw out a dry pastry tart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' looks like the pastry, but it is the adjective for sharp-tasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Arid land has little or no rain, so it is dry.

clue.text: Sailor's season

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to add flavour to food

explanation.walkthrough: 'Season' reads as a time of year, but it is the verb for flavouring food.
explanation.definitionFit: An old salt is a veteran sailor, and to salt food is to season it.

clue.text: Immortal doctor altering Triple Alliance

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the next word is reworked

parts.note: immortal means living for ever, eternal
the letters of altering rearranged

explanation.surface: An undying physician changing a historic European pact.
explanation.walkthrough: The Triple Alliance was a real 1882 pact of Germany, Austria-Hungary and Italy, but here it is a romantic arrangement. 'Doctor' looks like a noun, but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An eternal triangle is a love affair involving three people, wittily recast as a three-way alliance.

clue.text: Tenor seeks work

definitions.note: plural noun sense: pieces of work

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for tenor
to ask for something is to seek it

explanation.surface: A tenor singer is looking for employment.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasks are pieces of work to be done, so they stand for work in the sense of jobs.

clue.text: Pursued by dog, team head off

indicators.note: something pursued has another thing coming after it, so the later word goes first

parts.note: a side is a team
to dog someone is to follow or track them

explanation.surface: With a dog chasing them, a team's captain heads away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' looks like an animal, but it is the verb for following. 'Head off' looks like a team leader leaving; it is the verb for diverting.
explanation.definitionFit: To head off someone is to divert them from their course, which is what sidetrack means.
